title: O Lord, Our Father, Thanks to Thee
description: O Lord, Our Father, Thanks to Thee in Tonic Solfa to ES IST DAS HEIL UNS KOMMEN HER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Cyriacus Schneegass wrote these words in German. August Crull's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 170.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked 8.7.8.7.8.8.7, to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ES IST DAS HEIL UNS KOMMEN HER; any other 8.7.8.7.8.8.7 tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Lord, our Fa-ther, thanks to Thee In this new year we ren_-der, For Thou hast been from mis-e-ry And dan-gers our De-fend_-er; Through all the year that now has fled Hast given us life and dail-y bread And peace with-in our bor_-ders.

lines: O Lord, our Father, thanks to Thee
In this new year we render,
For Thou hast been from misery
And dangers our Defender;
Through all the year that now has fled
Hast given us life and daily bread
And peace within our borders.
Lord Jesus Christ, our thanks to Thee
In this new year we render,
For Thou still rulest zealously
Thy fold, with mercy tender;
Thou hast redeemed us with Thy blood,
Thou art our only Trust and Good,
In life and death our Savior.
Lord Holy Ghost, our thanks to Thee
In this new year we render,
For by Thy grace it is that we
Enjoy Thy Word’s pure splendor;
Thus Thou hast kindled from above
Within our hearts true faith and love
And other Christian virtues.
Our faithful God, we cry to Thee:
Still bless us with Thy favor,
Blot out all our iniquity,
And hide our sins forever;
Grant us a happy, good New Year
And, when the hour of death draws near,
A blest departure. Amen.

licence: Public domain: Cyriacus Schneegass died in 1597; August Crull died in 1923.
credits: Words by Cyriacus Schneegass (1546–1597), translated by August Crull (1845–1923), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ES IST DAS HEIL UNS KOMMEN HER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
